source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-63: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 63 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assumptions: use a declared model/tokenizer, context and output-length distributions, request mix, concurrency and offered load, batching, cache warmth, GPU/node/NIC topology, RDMA configuration, software versions, tenant policy, and quality/deadline thresholds; pin and verify all versions because Dynamo capabilities are release-specific. Hypothesis for corpus-05688: at matched output quality and offered load, the proposed disaggregated path improves the predeclared target (for example p95 TTFT or throughput) without violating p99 ITL, end-to-end p99, timeout/error rate, correctness, isolation, or cost bounds. diagnosis must begin with a trace-based symptom split (frontend, queue, prefill, KV transfer, decode, or RDMA) and use controlled fault injection rather than assuming a Dynamo defect. Compare co-located serving, disaggregation without KV movement where meaningful, and the complete path using randomized repeated trials across prompt-length, load, warm/cold-cache, and topology strata. Record frontend admission/routing and queue time; scheduler decisions; prefill/decode compute; KV schema, model/layer/shape/dtype/position compatibility; serialization, bytes, transfer latency and retries; RDMA counters; queue depth; GPU/NIC utilization; TTFT, ITL, end-to-end latency, throughput, token counts, errors, retries, cancellations, and output correctness, all with units and synchronized timestamps. Predeclare the effect size, sample size, percentile/uncertainty method, exclusion rules, and rollback gates. Control model, prompts, traffic generator, batching, replica count, placement, clocking, and background load; report confidence intervals and raw per-request traces. Inject worker loss, stale or corrupt/incompatible KV, RDMA/link degradation, timeout, queue overload, and control-plane failure. Reject invalid KV and unauthorized cross-tenant data; fence failed workers, bound retries, preserve correctness, drain or route around unhealthy stages, and fall back to a safe co-located path only within a tested capacity budget. Stop or roll back on quality regression, isolation violation, unbounded queue growth, error/timeout breach, or any SLO/cost gate failure. No improvement claim is supported until the pinned configuration, matched baselines, correctness checks, and fault evidence are measured.
risks: NVIDIA Dynamo behavior and interfaces may differ by unverified release or deployment.
Load, cache warmth, placement, batching, topology, and contention can confound stage attribution.
Fallback, KV integrity, authorization, and fault recovery require direct evidence under injected failures.
evidence_required: Pinned release, model, topology, network, and complete deployment configuration.
Matched baseline and ablation runs with synchronized per-request traces and raw counters.
Correctness, latency, throughput, resource, error, isolation, and fault-injection measurements with uncertainty.
